summary: Seven-study synthesis on the project physics (model v4 = v3 + optics overrides, era J/op slope, fab-limited doubling time T_d' = T_d + ln2·I·a, refresh-limited growth B_ss = D_cap·L/(1−ρ), cumulative mining, era presets and techAt). Four eras (2026 reference = v3, 2040, 2070, 2100+) with low/mid/high bundles. Mid hardware: hybrid 1.37 -> 1.04 -> 0.63 -> 0.555 g/W; FLOP per J of sunlight 1.6e12 -> 1.5e13 -> 6.8e13 -> 1.3e14; sail at f=0.01 0.919 -> 0.887 -> 0.855 -> 0.852 AU (sub-bandgap reflection, not hot chips); every era's sails stay inside 1 AU for f <= 0.1 and cross it only at f = 0.31-0.48. A cohort simulation with timeline-linked hardware (seed 2050) gives: heat wall 2109 (low 2196, high 2101), 1 % 2117, 10 % 2238, and a refresh-set ceiling of ~22 % (8-48 %) at 0.91 AU with 1.1e40 FLOP/s; Mercury's rock shell is used up by ~3127. Essentially all of the built swarm (> 99.99999 %) is 2100+ hardware, so the visualizer should show one mature era with a 2026 comparison and an outlook selector rather than a technology timeline. Invariants: film >> pods per kg (4.5-7.7x), Tj 85 C, Si-only PV, 279 m sail as the synchronous unit, heat-capped export. Flips: pods 15 % -> 1 %, HBM never flies, fabs set pre-wall growth, linear growth -> saturation, 64 -> 12 terminals, photonic lanes, 80x FLOP per joule.

eras.name: 2026 reference
eras.notes: Reference = model v3 exactly (the existing tests pin it): 7.8e-14 J/FLOP, 20 % AM0 c-Si at -0.42 %/K, alpha 0.90, 0.172 kg/m2, 64 x 10 cm terminals, 15 % HBM/DRAM pods, no fab limit, no refresh. Low/high vary only J/op (1.6e-13 / 4e-14 system) and pod share (20 % / 10 %). `corrected` holds what the future studies found wrong with the 2026 numbers themselves (thin-IBC tempco -0.34 %/K, design-spec stack 0.203 kg/m2, 2.2e-5 kg/W of terminals): 1.04 g/W sail instead of 0.92. Nobody builds a swarm with 2026 parts (first launch 2045-2060); this era is the comparison baseline.
conflicts_resolved: g/W: design spec 0.98 g/W (1.07 with 10 % overbuild) vs model 0.92 g/W (with overbuild). Like for like the gap is 0.15 g/W (16 %), not ~0.5 g/W: the spec film is 0.1905 kg/m2 + 0.0124 structure = 0.203 vs 0.172, because a 5 um back enamel only reaches eps 0.61 and the spec carries 15 um (+0.027 kg/m2). Kept 0.172 in the reference (tests), recorded 0.203 as ERAS[0].corrected and rebased every future era on the spec stack.

pvTempCo: -0.42 %/K is a legacy Voc 0.60 V cell; the 30 um IBC film is -0.34 %/K (study 4). Not applied to the reference (it moves the pinned 233 W/m2 to 244), applied in `corrected` and in all later eras (-0.29/-0.26 %/K).
energyPerKg: constants.js 255 MJ/kg vs study 6 1,150 MJ/kg (space-native fab): reference keeps 255 (v3 behaviour), later eras use study 6.

eras.notes: Seed-era hardware (first launch ~2050; the first ~4-7 doublings fly Earth-made chiplets). J/op 1.0e-14 system (IRDS x3.5, FP4, 3D/NVM locality); 1 GB NVM per chiplet possible but die area right-sized (22.5 mm2/W) for fab-limited growth; 22.5 % AM0 at -0.29 %/K; alpha 0.85 (first sub-bandgap reflectors); 0.185 kg/m2; ~12 terminals (8 x 10 cm + 4 x 30 cm, 6.2e-6 kg/W); photonic express lanes nascent; HBM gone (memory on logic in pods); pods 12.7 % (agent sandboxes still need DRAM cores); space-native wafer fab I = 40 kg per m2/yr; 10-yr life, 90 % recycled. Practically none of the visible swarm is built with these parts (2.4e-8 of all production is pre-2095).
conflicts_resolved: Pod share: study 2 (memory) 5 %, study 3 (interconnect) 1.5 %, study 5 combined p50 12.7 % (p90 24.5 %, 19.8 % if chiplets cannot run sandboxes). Study 5 is max(memory, workload) + special + 0.5 x switching, so it already contains 2 and 3: mid 12.7 %, high 5 % (study 2 floor), low 24.5 % (p90).

Fab tool intensity: study 6 lists I = 40 for 2040 but its effective T_d = 1.16 assumes panel imprint + DSA (I x area = 9). Mid uses I = 40 with right-sized die (T_d 1.54), high uses 9 (T_d 1.19), low 120 with 1 GB/chiplet die (T_d 2.23).
Film stack: study 4 gives 0.155 kg/m2 by subtracting its thinning steps from the model 0.172; applied to the design-spec stack (0.203) the same steps give 0.185 (mid). Study 4 value = high level.

eras.notes: Exponential-phase hardware (2060-2094), capital/fab-limited. J/op 2.6e-15; on-film photonic lanes make the 279 m sail one synchronous ~23 MW machine (2050-2070); 8 GB NVM/chiplet possible; 24 % AM0 at -0.26 %/K; alpha 0.80; eps 0.86/0.93; packing 0.93; 0.170 kg/m2; pods 2.6 % (sandboxes move onto MRAM/FeRAM chiplets); pod wings 0.125 kg/m2, module 1.2 kg/kW; I = 15; 10-yr life, 94 % recycled. Built while the swarm covers < 1e-5 of the Sun: invisible.
conflicts_resolved: Adiabatic logic (study 1: x2.1 energy, 611 mm2/W of silicon) vs study 4 (film offers only 1,840-2,440 mm2/W at the higher W/m2) and study 6 (die = 21 % of film area, tool intensity 0.35 needed): excluded at every level; adiabaticGain stays 1 (key kept for wildcards).
Tj: study 4 FLOP/s/kg optimum 95-125 C (within 2-6 %) vs study 1 (85 C every era) and the sunlight-limit argument: 85 C at every level; Tj 105/125 C are sensitivities.
Pod radiators: study 4 suggests 100 C, but study 2 keeps DRAM (85-95 C) as the reason pods exist: 80 C kept.

eras.notes: The hardware of the built swarm. J/op 1.4e-15 (within ~2x of the ~7e-16 irreversible floor, which mid reaches only if improvement continues to ~2200: x1.9 FLOP/s, no change in mass or coverage); 25 % AM0 c-Si near the Auger limit (30 % all-Si tandem only in high); alpha 0.80; 0.165 kg/m2; 20.9 mm chiplet pitch (1.6e8 chiplets, 23.9 MW, 1.7e22 FLOP/s per 279 m sail); 12 terminals (4.4e-6 kg/W); pods 1.1 % (dies > 3.8 W, write-heavy DRAM, cryostats, glass archives), wings 0.12 kg/m2, module 1.0 kg/kW; I = 5; life 15 yr (re-skin), 94 % recycled in orbit; 1,250 MJ/kg.
conflicts_resolved: Where the swarm sits: study 4 puts the rock-limited swarm (4e22 kg) outside Earth at 1.11-1.24 AU; study 6 shows refresh caps the standing fleet at D_cap L/(1-rho) = 4e21-2.6e22 kg unless rho >= 0.99. With rho <= 0.97 the swarm stays refresh-limited at 8-48 % coverage and sits at 0.90-1.04 AU: inside Earth orbit in low and mid, crossing 1 AU only in high (~2990). The rock is consumed by refresh losses over ~1,000 yr instead.
Refresh: study 6 headline (L 10, rho 0.94) vs its era table (rho 0.97 by 2100+, L 15-20 after ~2150): mid L 15, rho 0.94; high L 20, rho 0.97; low L 10, rho 0.90.

Memory: workloads (study 5) want 8-32 GB per chiplet for agents; manufacturing (study 6) wants the useful minimum (1.65 GB) because capacity costs fab area. Resolved by phase: right-sized die (21.6 mm2/W) while fabs set growth, agent-sized NVM on post-wall refresh production where mass binds (fab stock rises from 1.3 % to ~3 % of the fleet; using 32 GB during growth delays the single-era wall ~9 yr).

Pod mass: study 4 tables kept 2026 pods (4.0 g/W); its own parameter list (wing 0.12 kg/m2, 1.0 kg/kW) gives 2.5 g/W, used here; each 1 % of power in pods then adds 3.6 % to swarm mass, not the 7.4 % quoted in study 5.

timeline.method: Cohort simulation (sim.mjs). Each cohort carries the hardware of its build year from techAt(year, level) (era presets interpolated: J/op, laser mass and fab intensity log-linear, the rest linear; held at 2100+ afterwards). Gross production = min(capital x ln2/T_d', D_cap + rho x retirements) with T_d' = 1 yr + ln2 x I x a of the hardware being built; D_cap = 3.94e19 kg/yr delivered (Mercury heat cap); cohorts retire at their era's service life; rho of retired mass is recycled in orbit; new Mercury mass stops when the crust+mantle (8.0e22 kg rock, 4.0e22 kg delivered) is used up. Coverage solved each step from every cohort's kg per W of sunlight at the current coverage (thermal placement). Seed 1e6 kg in 2050.
timeline.closed_form_check: The closed form in hybrid.js v4 with 2100+ mid parts (wall 2102, 1 % 2110, 10 % 2235, ceiling 22.2 %) matches the cohort simulation (wall 2108.6, 1 % 2117, 10 % 2238, peak 21.7 %) within ~7 yr; the gap is the slower 2050-2095 hardware before the wall.

variants.label: mid, L = 10 yr and rho = 0.94 in every era

mid, J/op keeps falling to the irreversible floor (7.3e-16 J system) by 2200

reachable_coverage.answer: Central (mid): the swarm hits Mercury's heat wall in 2109, covers 1 % of the Sun in 2117, 5 % in 2162, 10 % in 2238 and 20 % in 2651, then levels off at ~22 % (1.1e+40 FLOP/s, sails at 0.92 AU, inside Earth's orbit) as the standing fleet approaches B_ss = D_cap L/(1-rho) = 9.9e21 kg. The ceiling is set by service life and recycling, not by Mercury's heat or mass. The crust and mantle are used up by ~3127 (refresh losses keep digging at the full heat-limited rate); after that the fleet decays at (1-rho)/L = 0.4 %/yr unless core metal or asteroids feed it (7.7 % coverage by 3400).

range.low: wall 2196, 1 % in 2204, 5 % in 2283, ceiling ~8 % (L 10 yr, rho 0.90; T_d ~3 yr with a space wafer fab at I = 40 and 32 GB chiplets)

levers: Recycling and life: no recycling caps the mid swarm at 1.5 % (2026 parts and L = 10: 0.57 %); L 10 / rho 0.94 everywhere gives 15 %; the rock-limited 4e22 kg swarm needs rho >= 0.99.
Fab productivity: no fab limit moves the wall to 2096 (-13 yr); 2026-style fabs (I = 250) forever move it to ~2886 and 1 % to ~2867.
Sandboxes on chiplets: if they cannot host agent sandboxes (pods ~15 %), the ceiling drops from 21.7 % to 15.6 % (-28 %) and 10 % slips from 2238 to 2334.
Seed date: a 2060 seed shifts everything by ~8 yr; a 10-yr hardware lag shifts the wall by ~2.5 yr.
reachable_coverage.never: With any level studied, a closed shell (f = 1) or the rock-limited swarm is not reached; 50 % needs rho >~ 0.98 with 20-yr lives.

dominant_era.answer: 2100+. Of all spacecraft mass ever produced in the mid timeline, 2.4e-8 is built before 2095 (2070-era parts) and 1.7e-16 before 2060 (2040-era parts); 2100+ parts are >99.99999 % of production and of mass-years in orbit (high: 1.6e-6 pre-2095; low: 7e-13). The exponential puts most of the pre-wall mass into the last few doublings (2096-2109), and refresh replaces every sail every 10-20 yr, so from ~2125 more than half of all output is replacement and the standing fleet is always 0-L years old (mean hardware age ~6-8 yr in 2150-3000).
dominant_era.why_not_2070: Everything built in the 2060-2094 window (1.5e16 kg) covers < 1e-5 of the Sun and is retired by ~2105. 2070-era parts are at most 4 % of the fleet in 2100 (still invisible: f = 9e-6), 0 % by 2110.
dominant_era.caveat: Calendar labels assume first launch 2050 and no lag between Earth roadmaps and Mercury fabs; a 10-yr lag or a 2060 seed changes none of this. If J/op keeps improving after 2100 (to ~7.3e-16 J by ~2200), the built swarm is "2100-2200" hardware with up to 1.9x the FLOP/s of the 2100+ preset at the same mass, coverage and orbit.
dominant_era.build_window: Bulk build 2096-3125 (heat wall to rock exhaustion); 2090-2300 contains the visible rise from 1e-6 to 13 % coverage, all of it 2100+ parts.

invariants: The film beats pods per kg in every era and level: sail FLOP/s/kg is 4.5-7.7x the pod value (film 0.36-0.92 g/W vs pods 2.4-3.9 g/W). The film share only grows.

The film temperature is set by absorptance, emissivity and coverage, never by PV efficiency: chiplets stay at Tj 85 C on a 348-349 K film in every era; the optimum Tj is flat 85-105 C, and hot logic (> ~150 C) never pays.
Thin c-Si (all-Si tandem at best) is the only swarm-scale absorber; perovskite and III-V are capped at f <= 1e-5 / 3e-6 by I, In and Ge.
Sparse swarms sit inside Earth's orbit (0.84-0.94 AU for f <= 0.1 at every level); a closed shell sits outside (1.32-1.35 AU). Sails cross 1 AU at f = 0.31 (2026 parts) to 0.48 (2100+ high).
The sail stays 150-300 m (279 m, 69,543 m2) and is the synchronous unit; chiplets stay 0.15 W (spreader mass ~P^2); only the pitch shrinks (26.8 -> 20.9 mm mid).
After the heat wall Mercury exports 3.94e19 kg/yr in every era (5e18 W surface cap at 2 MJ/kg); this holds only if refineries and fabs leave the surface by model year ~40-60 (~2090-2110).
Refresh, not Mercury's heat or rock, sets how much swarm can stand at once (B_ss = D_cap L/(1-rho)); without recycling the swarm never reaches ~1.5 %.
Making the swarm costs a few % of its output: processing power 0.4-2.7 % of chip power at the wall, energy payback 3-43 days, even at 1,000-5,000 MJ/kg.
The swarm is invisible (< 1e-5 of the Sun) for its first ~40-105 years (mid: until ~2096-2100) and visible only with 2100+ hardware.

Earth's energy budget depends on coverage and orbit, not on technology: an interior swarm at 1 % adds ~1.9 W/m2 of forcing at Earth (0.5 CO2 doublings), ~20 W/m2 at 10 % and ~49 W/m2 at the 22 % mid ceiling (model v1/v3 earthImpact, unchanged here).
Pods never sit inside the sail shell, and pods exist only for jobs the film cannot do (DRAM-bound CPU work, > 3.8 W dies, cryostats, archives) - never for synchronous work.
The byte across 1 AU costs ~1e7 FLOP-equivalents in every era, and per-layer collectives never cross sails (light time 0.15-1 ms to neighbours).

model_changes: hybrid.js v4 (proposed file) keeps every v3 default and output: 1,620 compared values identical (equiv.mjs), the 7 v3 tests pass unchanged, and 32/32 tests pass in a repo copy with the proposed test file.

New PARAMS: hotLogicSlope (energy-per-op slope above 85 C, default = 2026 table), adiabaticGain (film J/op divisor, default 1), alpha (film solar absorptance, default 0.90), laserKgPerW (default 2e-5), fabToolIntensity (kg per m2/yr of die, default 0 = off), dieMm2PerW (default 40), serviceLife (yr, default 0 = never retired), recycleFrac (default 0), energyPerKg (MJ/kg, default 255).

Optional overrides without sliders: epsFront, epsBack, packing (via filmOptics(p) on top of FIXED.film), podDieMm2PerW (FIXED.podDieMm2PerW 3.3), chipAreaPerKg (forces a), seedYear (FIXED.seedYear 2050).
Default sailArea 1e6 m2 -> 69,543 m2 (design-spec 279 m sail; affects counts only; no test depends on it).
energyPenalty(tjC, slope): rescales the 2026 table as E^(slope/0.00912); the 2100+ value 0.0056 gives 1.12 at 105 C and 1.25 at 125 C (E ~ T^2).

swarmAt(p, f) splits the physics from compute(); coverageForMass(p, m) inverts mass(f); compute() adds steadyCoverage, flopsPerWsun, flopsPerKgRock and an industry block (chipAreaPerKg, doublingYearsEff, processingShareAtWall, energyPaybackDays, factoriesOffMercuryYear, fabStockPerFleet).

growthPlan moves into hybrid.js: T_d' = T_d + ln2·I·a with a = ((1-q) dieMm2PerW + q podDie)·1e-6 / (kg per chip W); after the wall B(t) = B_ss - (B_ss - B_cap) exp(-(1-rho)(t - t_cap)/L), B_ss = D_cap L/(1-rho); new fields doublingYearsEff, fabPenaltyYears, refresh, steadyMass, refreshTimeConstant, reachableMass/Fraction, yearsToEnd (finite timeline end), yearsToSteady90, builtAtYear, deliveredBy. yearsToFull and yearsForMass return Infinity beyond the ceiling.
atYear: mercuryRemoved/radius/surface use cumulative export (deliveredBy), exportRate continues at (1-rho)B/L after completion, new retireRate, replacementShare, processingPower, calendarYear.
ERAS (2026, 2040, 2070, 2100+) with mid/low/high overrides and a 2026 `corrected` set; eraParams(key, level); techAt(year, level) interpolates anchors (log for J/op, laser mass, fab intensity).
Bug fix: podFrac = 0 with infeasible pods gave NaN mass (0 x Infinity) in v3.

Recommended but not applied to the 2026 reference (they change pinned numbers): pvTempCo -0.0034 (W/m2 233 -> 244), filmAreal 0.203 (design spec) or a thin high-eps emitter, laserKgPerW 2.2e-5, INDUSTRY.energyPerKg 255e6 -> 1150e6 in constants.js (used by model.js v1).

UI (not changed here): main.js still runs model.js v1, not hybrid.js. When wiring v4: timeScale must use growth.yearsToEnd (yearsToFull can be Infinity), the initial year falls back when yearsTo10pct is Infinity, the "complete" and "mantle gone" milestones need deliveredBy, and the Mercury scene should show cumulative mining.

visualizer_recommendation.choice: One mature era (2100+ mid) for everything the viewer can see, with a 2026 comparison, and a pessimistic/central/optimistic outlook selector. Do not animate hardware along the timeline.
visualizer_recommendation.why: The hardware changes only while the swarm is invisible: before the heat wall (~2109) it covers < 3e-3 of the Sun, and > 99.99999 % of all spacecraft ever built carry 2100+ parts (refresh keeps the fleet 0-15 yr old). A timeline-linked technology curve would change the numbers only during decades when the scene shows nothing, and era presets as a time axis would suggest a 2040 or 2070 swarm that never exists.
how: Default parameters = eraParams("2100", "mid"); an "Outlook" control switches low/mid/high (moves the wall 2101-2196, 1 % 2107-2204, ceiling 8-48 %).

A "2026 parts" toggle (or a ledger column) shows what the same swarm would be with today's hardware: 1.37 vs 0.555 g/W, 1.6e12 vs 1.3e14 FLOP per J of sunlight, 0.92 vs 0.85 AU, and that 2026 fabs would push the heat wall to ~2886.

Calendar years on the timeline (first launch 2050), model years secondary. Milestones: first visible (1e-6, ~2096), heat wall (~2109), 1 % (~2117), 10 % (~2238), refresh ceiling (~22 %, approached from ~2650), rock shell gone (~3127).

Replace the linear post-wall growth with the refresh curve; mark "complete" only if the target is below the ceiling; cap the coverage slider at the ceiling with a note on what recycling would raise it.
Use techAt() only for ledger text about the pre-wall decades ("sails launched in 2070 carry 2.6e-15 J/FLOP chips"), not for the 3D scenes.
Mercury: show cumulative mining (4.6 % of the planet by 2300); factories move off the surface by ~2090-2110 (co-orbital foundry ring); refresh depots appear in the swarm shell after ~2110.

sail: Same 279 m diamond, booms, hub, corner vanes and 1.63 m hinge strips: sail size is set by structure, not technology.
Back face: denser chiplet grid, 2.45 mm dies at 20.9 mm pitch (was 25.4-26.8 mm); ~1.6e8 chiplets per sail.

Remove the 60 patch terminals on 0.6 m masts and their 1 x 1 m service plates. Show ~12 terminals: 8 small 10 cm units (0.3 x 0.3 x 0.75 m) at boom tips and hub, 4 larger 30 cm units (~0.45 x 0.45 x 1.0 m with a 0.4 m sunshade tube) on hub service plates, each with a 0.07-0.3 m2 radiator plate (bright in LWIR at 300-330 K).

Photonic express lanes: an orthogonal grid of 2-20 mm fibre bundles under the back enamel every 1-3 m, crossing hinge strips as continuous loops; visible only in close-ups as a faint grazing-angle sheen.
Front face: unchanged near-black navy in visible light (sub-bandgap reflector, alpha 0.80, is invisible to the eye; in a near-IR view the film is bright, reflectance 0.6-0.8 above 1.1 um).
Thermal view: film still 349 K, chiplets 358 K (the film temperature does not change with era).
Per sail: 23.9 MW of chips, 1.7e22 FLOP/s (~0.55x all AI compute on Earth in 2025).
Swarm scenes: sails at 0.85 AU early, 0.91 AU at the ceiling (inside Earth's orbit); ~1/15 of sails replaced per year, so a few in a thousand are rolled up or dark at any time beside depot craft.
pod: Pods are rare: ~1 % of chip power (roughly one 1 MW pod per 4 sails by count, tiny by area). No training-island clusters (the sail is the training island); no switch or gateway pods (relay craft with 1 m telescopes, one per 1e5-1e7 sails, never two in a frame).
Module: memory bonded on logic, no HBM stacks; same knife-edge radiators at 80 C (pods remain DRAM-bound); lighter wings (0.12 kg/m2) and module (1.0 kg/kW): pod 2.5 g/W instead of 3.9.
If the 15 % no-sandbox branch is shown, pods return to today's share and layout.

headline_numbers.detail: set by sail life and in-orbit recycling (B = export x life / (1 - recycled)), approached over centuries; 1.1e40 FLOP/s at 0.91 AU

headline_numbers.label: Mercury dug
headline_numbers.detail: all of the crust and mantle by ~3127; then the swarm shrinks

headline_numbers.label: Pods
headline_numbers.detail: 15 % if film chiplets cannot host agent sandboxes (costs 28 % of the ceiling)

headline_numbers.label: Inside Earth's orbit
headline_numbers.detail: sails cross 1 AU only above ~46 % coverage

open_questions: In-orbit recycling fraction and service life dominate the final swarm (8-48 %); no data exist for recycling c-Si/Mg/glass films in orbit at 90-97 %.

Whether an area-parallel patterning process (panel imprint + inorganic self-assembly, 9-15 nm) reaches 3-15 kg of tools per m2/yr: it sets the heat wall between 2100 and ~2200 (and ~2886 at 2026 productivity).
Whether film chiplets get sandbox-capable cores with MMU and NVM main memory (pods 1 % vs 15 %, ceiling 21.7 % vs 15.6 %).
Film stack: design spec 0.203 kg/m2 (15 um enamel) vs a thin high-emissivity emitter (0.135-0.17): +-20 % on g/W in every era.
What feeds the swarm after the rock shell is gone (~3127): Mercury's core metal is not PV material; asteroids or Venus would change the long run.

An interior swarm at the ~22 % ceiling puts ~49 W/m2 of extra forcing on Earth (model earthImpact); a sunlight corridor or an exterior placement (Tj 116-141 C) has a price (16-63 % of compute, study 4).
J/op after 2100: the irreversible floor (~7e-16 J) would double FLOP/s at the same mass; reversible logic stays fab-limited (adiabatic g = 6 pushes the wall to ~2540).
The pre-wall decades are modelled with no lag between Earth roadmaps and Mercury fabs, and with Earth-imported chiplets ignored for the first ~4-7 doublings; both shift dates by only a few years.
Pod mass by era: study 4's tables (4.0 g/W) and its parameter list (2.5 g/W) disagree; with ~1 % pods it changes swarm mass by < 2 %.
Refineries and fabs must leave Mercury's surface by model year ~40-60; the co-orbital foundry ring (1e18-6e18 m2 of radiators) is not modelled.
levels_note: low = slow progress, high = fast progress; coherent pessimistic/optimistic bundles (an envelope), not joint percentiles. Tj 85 C at every level so orbits stay comparable.
